newsitem.title: FRANCE: Police detain 11 in Corsica separatist raids.
newsitem.headline: Police detain 11 in Corsica separatist raids.

text.p: Police detained 11 people on Monday in a string of raids on Corsican nationalists in southern France and on the Mediterranean island, judicial sources said.

But police found no weapons, bomb-making equipment or illegal documents in the swoops. The sources said some of the main suspects had slipped away before the police arrived, apparently helped by tip-offs.

Eleven people -- seven men and four women -- were placed in custody after the raids ordered by an anti-terrorism magistrate in mainland France, Balagne in the north-west of Corsica and areas of the south-east of the island.
Seven people were detained in Corsica, four in the southern French cities of Marseille, Aix-en-Provence and Toulon.

Hardline Corsican separatists have recently stepped up their 20-year-old campaign for greater autonomy from mainland France with a spate of mostly night-time bombings and machine-gunnings of government buildings or police stations on the island.
Monday's raids targeted members of Cuncolta Naziunalista, the legal wing of the banned Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC), the sources said.
Balagne is a stronghold of Jean-Michel Rossi, editor of U Ribombu, a leading nationalist publication.

Francois Santoni, head of Cuncolta, and his lawyer girlfriend Marie-Helene Mattei were placed under investigation last month for attempted extortion, complicity in bomb attacks and membership of a terrorist organisation.
